title: ProductAvailability
description: TOGAF-sourced quality archetype — Availability viability dimension. Defines the property vocabulary for availability governance: uptime targets, recovery objectives, redundancy. Rootless archetype (no structural allOf) — used as qualifier in Directives/Norms and as data type for Effectors/Receptors carrying availability state. Norm predicates reference properties by Availability.{property} in CEL expressions. Source framework: TOGAF (Architecture Principles, Non-Functional Requirements) + ISO/IEC 25010 (Availability sub-characteristic).

uptimePercent.description: Service availability as a percentage (e.g., 99.99). Norm example: Availability.uptimePercent >= 99.9.

recoveryTimeObjective.description: Maximum acceptable duration to restore service after failure (ISO 8601 duration, e.g., 'PT15M' for 15 minutes).

recoveryPointObjective.description: Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time (ISO 8601 duration, e.g., 'PT1H' for 1 hour of data loss tolerance).

maintenanceWindowDuration.description: Planned maintenance window duration (ISO 8601 duration, e.g., 'PT4H').

redundancyMode.description: Infrastructure redundancy topology. NONE = single instance. ACTIVE_PASSIVE = standby failover. ACTIVE_ACTIVE = load-balanced replicas. MULTI_REGION = geo-distributed.
